salient_findings: Erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions on the face, chest, abdomen, and limbs
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein
key_facts: The patient is a child weighing 30 kg
The patient has no comorbidities or allergies

The patient has erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions on the face, chest, abdomen, and limbs
The patient reported frequent contact with stray cats

Erythrocyte sedimentation rate is 47 mm/h

IgE level is 7200 μg/L

raw.rationale: Mycological culture yielded growth of Trichophyton mentagrophytes, which is a common cause of dermatophytosis, and the patient's symptoms of erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions are consistent with this diagnosis

rejected.label: Trichophyton infection
rejected.why: While Trichophyton mentagrophytes was isolated, the term 'Dermatophytosis' is more specific to the clinical presentation

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not specifically suggest erythema multiforme

rejected.label: Cat scratch disease
rejected.why: Although the patient reported contact with stray cats, the presence of Trichophyton mentagrophytes and the nature of the skin lesions point more towards a fungal infection

rejected.label: Erythema nodosum
rejected.why: The patient's skin lesions are described as well-demarcated and located on multiple areas, which is not typical of erythema nodosum

gold: Dermatophyte infection due to Trichophyton interdigitale
